candidates.angle: Maharathah, the great warriors, will think you fled from fear

candidates.angle: Those who once held you in high regard will see you reduced to smallness

angle_en: Maharathah: how great warriors read fear
angle_hi: महारथाः: बड़े महारथी डर को कैसे देखते हैं

en.intro: What happens to a warrior's name when he stops fighting? Listen to how Krishna warns him that the great warriors will think he withdrew from battle out of fear.
en.notice: The word Maharathah means great chariot-warriors, and laabhavam means smallness or a drop in status. Those who once held him in high regard will see him reduced to nothing.
en.next: Krishna asks what could be more painful than enemies mocking a warrior's strength.
en.meaning: The great warriors will think you withdrew from battle out of fear. Those who once held you in high regard will see you as small.

hi.intro: जब कोई योद्धा लड़ना छोड़ देता है, तो उसके नाम का क्या होता है? सुनिए, कैसे श्रीकृष्ण चेतावनी देते हैं कि बड़े बड़े महारथी उसे डर के कारण युद्ध से हटता हुआ मानेंगे।
hi.meaning: महारथी लोग यही सोचेंगे कि तुम डर के कारण युद्ध से हट गए। जो लोग कभी तुम्हें बहुत सम्मान देते थे, वे तुम्हें छोटे होते हुए देखेंगे।
hi.notice: महारथाः का अर्थ है बड़े महारथी और लाघवम् का अर्थ है छोटी हैसियत। जो लोग कभी तुम्हें बहुत सम्मान देते थे, वे तुम्हें छोटे होते हुए देखेंगे।
hi.next: श्रीकृष्ण पूछते हैं कि शत्रुओं के द्वारा किसी योद्धा की ताकत का मज़ाक उड़ाए जाने से अधिक कष्टदायक और क्या हो सकता है।

issues: meaning_changed: "तुम्हारी करुणा को लोग कायरता ही समझेंगे" (The Hindi meaning adds the word 'people' (लोग) and explicitly states 'your compassion will be understood as cowardice' (तुम्हारी करुणा को लोग कायरता ही समझेंगे), which is a specific interpretation not present in the source or the standard translation. The source says 'they will think you withdrew from battle out of fear' (मंस्यन्ते त्वां भयाद्रणादुपरतम्), without mentioning 'cowardice' or 'people'.)

meaning_changed: "जिन लोगों की नज़र में तुम अब तक बहुत सम्मानित थे, उनकी नज़र में तुम छोटे हो जाओगे।" (The source specifies that the loss of status comes from 'those who once held you in high regard' (येषां च त्वं बहुमतो भूत्वा). The Hindi phrase 'जिन लोगों की नज़र में तुम अब तक बहुत सम्मानित थे' (Those who were very respected in whose view until now) shifts the timing to the present/ongoing respect, and more critically, omits the causal link 'having become' (भूत्वा) and 'will go' (यास्यसि). It turns a future loss of status into a present state, slightly altering the temporal logic and softening the warning of a future fall.)

meaning_changed: "अर्जुन की करुणा को कायरता मानेंगे" (The intro and notice state that the great warriors will view Arjuna's 'compassion' (karuna) as cowardice. The source verse 35 does not mention Arjuna's compassion (karuna) at all; it explicitly states that the great warriors will think he withdrew from battle 'out of fear' (bhayat). The Hindi bhavarth also introduces the word 'karuna' (compassion), which is not in the source.)
